chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Aban, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
Al-mula'ana (mutual cursing/divorce) and al-ila' (oath of abstinence) do not occur except after consummation (entry).

key_terms.الدُّخُولِ: Dakhul, consummation of marriage, specifically the entry into the marital bed.
key_terms.الْإِيلَاءُ: Al-iila', an oath by the husband to abstain from sexual relations with his wife for four months.
key_terms.الْمُلَاعَنَةُ: Al-mula'ana, a form of divorce involving mutual cursing, typically when a husband accuses his wife of zina without four witnesses.

ai.seo_question: When do al-mula'ana and al-ila' apply in Shia Islamic law?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies a key procedural condition in Shia fiqh, asserting that both al-mula'ana (mutual cursing divorce) and al-ila' (oath of abstinence) are legally contingent upon the consummation of the marriage (dakhul). This distinction is significant because it differentiates these mechanisms from other forms of divorce that may apply even before consummation, ensuring the legal status of the wife is properly established. The ruling underscores the precision of Shia jurists in linking specific marital obligations and penalties to the physical reality of the marital bond.
